elements.element: The obligations apply upon expiry of the Agreement.
elements.evidence: Section 4.3 applies expressly “[u]pon expiration ... of this Agreement.”

elements.element: The obligations apply upon termination of the Agreement.
elements.evidence: Section 4.3 applies expressly upon “termination of this Agreement for any reason.”

elements.element: Vendor must provide transition assistance to Customer.
elements.evidence: HDI must “provide the Company with transition assistance.”

elements.element: Transition assistance must be available for up to six months following expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: The clause guarantees assistance only for “at least ninety (90) days” and does not establish a right to assistance for a requested period of up to six months.

elements.element: Transition assistance must be provided at Vendor's then-current rates.
elements.evidence: The clause does not specify any rates or other charges for transition assistance.

elements.element: Vendor must return Customer Data to Customer.
elements.evidence: HDI must export and deliver to the Company “all Content, user information and other data of the Company,” which substantively covers Customer Data.

elements.element: Customer Data must be returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: The clause requires export and delivery but specifies no standard or machine-readable format.

elements.element: Customer Data must be returned within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: HDI must export and deliver the data “within thirty (30) days after such expiration or termination.”

elements.element: Vendor must delete Customer Data after returning it.
elements.evidence: No deletion obligation appears in the operative language.

elements.element: Vendor must certify its deletion of Customer Data.
elements.evidence: No deletion-certification obligation appears in the operative language.

elements.element: The fallback obligations apply upon expiry of the Agreement.
elements.evidence: Section 4.3 applies expressly “[u]pon expiration ... of this Agreement.”

elements.element: The fallback obligations apply upon termination of the Agreement.
elements.evidence: Section 4.3 applies expressly upon “termination of this Agreement for any reason.”

elements.element: Vendor must provide transition assistance to Customer.
elements.evidence: HDI must “provide the Company with transition assistance.”

elements.element: Transition assistance must be provided for 90 days following expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: The clause requires transition assistance “for a period of at least ninety (90) days following such expiration or termination.”

elements.element: Vendor must export and deliver Customer Data to Customer.
elements.evidence: HDI must “export and deliver to the Company all Content, user information and other data of the Company.”

elements.element: The data export must occur within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: The export and delivery must occur “within thirty (30) days after such expiration or termination.”

result.reason: The operative redline fully reaches the fallback by covering both expiry and termination, requiring at least 90 days of transition assistance, and requiring delivery of Company data within 30 days. It does not reach the preferred position because it omits the six-month assistance window, then-current rates, machine-readable format, deletion, and deletion certification. Unrelated termination and payment terms remain intact and no contradiction is introduced. The redline is not strictly minimal because “at least ninety (90) days” creates an uncapped assistance period rather than the fallback's defined 90-day period. Drafting quality is weak because that duration has no endpoint and the clause leaves transition-assistance scope and export format undefined.
